paper_title: Recurrent Axinovae and their Cosmological Constraints
suggested_experiment_name: Recurrent Axinovae cosmological constraint (T_osc-independent, M* ~ t^0.2)
coupling_convention: f_a^{-1} in GeV^-1 (inverse axion decay constant), exactly as plotted on the y-axis; x-axis is m_a in eV. Values NOT inverted or converted to f_a.
notes: Paper places new cosmological exclusion limits directly on the (m_a, f_a) plane from recurrent axion star explosions (axinovae) converting DM to dark radiation, using the decaying-DM bound f_dDM <= 2.62% (2-sigma, from Nygaard et al.). Coupling type is clearly AxionMass: constraints are independent of non-gravitational SM couplings and shown in Fig. 1 as exclusion regions spanning m_a ~ 1e-20 to 1e-4 eV with y-axis apparently 1/f_a in GeV^-1 (~1e-17 to 1e-7, i.e., f_a ~ 1e7-1e17 GeV). However, no numerical table or explicit limit values are given in the text; the exclusion contours exist only as unreadable figure regions, so no data points could be extracted. Bound assumes post-inflationary PQ breaking, axions comprising the DM, and white-noise isocurvature spectrum. The 2.62% constraint is quoted at 2-sigma (~95% CL). | selector: figure_vision (sole candidate) | Vision: Traced Fig. 2 (page 11): orange 'T_osc independent exclusion' region from recurrent axinovae converting axion DM to dark radiation. The plot axes are m_a [eV] (x) vs f_a^{-1} [GeV^-1] (y); excluded region lies ABOVE the boundary (large f_a^{-1} = small f_a = strong self-coupling). The boundary is a straight line on log-log with slope ~0.51 (approximately constant confinement scale Lambda = sqrt(m_a f_a)), so points are sampled uniformly. Gray regions (black-hole superradiance) are pre-existing limits and were not traced. Fig. 1 (page 6) shows alternative assumptions (green/red/blue regions); the blue optimized bound is similar to this Fig. 2 line. Assumes axions constitute the full DM relic abundance with post-inflationary (isocurvature) fluctuations.
